survey: A coral cluster on a low pile of rocks, standing on a flat sandy-green seabed. The camera is slightly above the scene and nearly level with it, with the floor's back edge as a horizontal line behind the cluster. A large purple-grey boulder sits in the center. Its top face shows a little, which fits the slightly raised view. Smaller grey and teal stones sit in front of it and at both sides. Each one shows a hint of its top surface and rests flat on the floor, with soft contact shadows. A big pink branching coral rises upright from behind the boulder, with an orange coral behind it on the left and another on the right. A magenta coral is tucked in front at the left, and a small red fan coral sits on the floor in front of the boulder. The corals are organic shapes with no rows, grids or round rims that would have to follow a surface. They spread mostly in the picture plane, which reads as a natural frontal view. The shading and overlaps put all the corals at consistent depths. Everything agrees on one slightly-above, nearly level viewpoint, and the ground meets every rock at the angle the floor is drawn.
